 Judgment

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.11,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 15-04-2023 at about 5.30 to 5.31 p.m., the petitioner was going to town along with her father Raju on the TVS Star City motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-03-HZ- 6787, being driven by her father, slowly, carefully and cautiously, by observing traffic rules, on Ramasagara- Muttalanur road.

At that time, near Ramasagara village,
Anekal Taluka, Bengaluru District, a Innova car bearing Reg. No.KL-56-P-0849,
driven by its driver with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, endangering the human life, came in the opposite direction and dashed to the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, she was shifted to N.H.
Hospital, wherein she took first aid treatment and then she was shifted to Sri Priya Nursing Home, Kuppam, wherein she took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident, the petitioner was student.
But, due to the accidental injuries, she has lost her memory and her bright future.
The Suryanagar Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.11,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.1 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.

Hence, the respondent No.2 is placed as ex-parte.
4.
The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for mis-joinder and non- joinder of parties.
The rider of the motorcycle was wholly and solely responsible for the alleged accident.
Consequently the owner and insurer of the same are a necessary parties in the present proceedings.
On the contrary, the driver of the Innova car bearing No.KL-56-P-0849 was no way responsible for the alleged accident.
Consequently the respondents are not a necessary parties.
But, still they have been made parties by the petitioner with ulterior intention.

It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.2, in respect of Innova car bearing Reg. No.KL-56-P-0849 vide policy bearing No.OG-23-16071801- 00000464 and its validity from 22-10-2023 to 21-10-2024.
Further it is contended that, the driver of the offending Innova car was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle at the time of alleged accident.

Hence, the respondent No.2 has violated the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act and also committed the breach of the terms and conditions of the policy by permitting the unlicensed driver to drive the said vehicle.
Hence, this respondent is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.

Further it is contended that, the Innova car bearing Reg. No.KL-56-P-0849 was used in a public place without having a valid permit and fitness certificate and thereby violated the terms and conditions of the contract of insurance policy and also against the provisions of Motor Vehicles Act.
It seeks protection under Section 149(2) of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.

It has denied the age of the petitioner,
injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by her.
Further, it has sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 15-04-2023 at about 5.30 p.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Innova Car bearing Reg.
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?

11. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 8, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Innova car bearing Reg. No.KL-56-P-0849 and dashing the same to oncoming motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-HZ-6787, in which the petitioner was traveling as pillion rider.
Due to said impact, the petitioner has fell down on the road and sustained grievous injury on her right thigh.

The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.8, has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Innova car bearing Reg. No.KL-56-P-0849.

At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
the issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.1 in respect of Innova car bearing Reg.
No.KL-56-P-0849 and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

Further, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/Respondents No.2, as he did not choose to appear and contest the case of the petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.1 has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-HZ-6787 and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of Innova car bearing Reg. No.KL-56-P-0849.
But, the respondent No.1 has failed to establish the said contentions.
It has neither adduced any evidence, nor it has produced any document to establish the above contentions.
Even, the respondents No.1 has not stepped into witness box to depose the said contentions on oath.

In such circumstances, there is absolutely no evidence on record to show that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-03-HZ-6787, in which the petitioner was traveling as a pillion rider.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Innova car bearing Reg. No.KL-56- P-0849 and dashing the same to the motorcycle of the petitioner.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-03- HZ-6787 or there was any contributory negligence on his part, in the cause of accident.
13.

Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazar also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the left side 20 feet vide Dommasandra-Chandapura road, near Ramasagara Village, Sarjapura Hobli, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru Urban District, in between the offending Innova car bearing Reg.
No.KL-56-P-0849 and oncoming motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-03-HZ-6787 of the petitioner.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.5, the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-03-HZ-6787,
then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.

Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.8 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Innova car bearing Reg. No.KL-56-P-0849 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injury in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the driver or the owner of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KL-56-P-0849.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records,
regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident,
negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

Therefore, in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, she has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 15-04-2023 at about 5.30 p.m., on Dommasandra-Chandapura road, near Ramasagara Village, Sarjapura Hobli, Anekal Taluk,
Bengaluru Urban District, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Innova car bearing Reg. No.KL-56- P-0849.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Innova car bearing Reg. No.KL-56-P-0849 and she has sustained grievous injury in the said accident.
As per the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, she has sustained fracture shaft of right femur and for the said injury she has undergone surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.
To prove her age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of her Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.15.
As per Ex.P.15, the date of birth of the petitioner is 07-01-2017.
The accident has taken place on 15-04-2023 at about 5.30 P.M.
This clearly goes to show that, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 6 years.
In the case in hand, petitioner is admittedly a minor of the age of 6 years as on the date of accident and she has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the above cited decision, the petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
21. Pain and suffering already undergone and to be suffered in future, mental and physical shock,
hardship, inconvenience, and discomforts, etc. and loss of amenities in life on account of permanent disability:
The petitioner has averred that due to accidental injuries, she has sustained grievous injuries and suffered physical disability.

Further, the P.W.3, who is the doctor, who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has sustained fracture shaft of right femur and for the said injury she has undergone surgery i.e. CRIF with TENS nailing under GA.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability of 32% to the right lower limb and 12% to the whole body.

The Ex.P.4 wound certificate,
Ex.P.9 discharge summary, Ex.P.13 x-ray, Ex.P.20 clinical notes and Ex.P.21 x-ray are clear evident that, the petitioner has suffered the above mentioned injury and she has undergone surgery for the said injury.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.3 in length

,
nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions that, the petitioner has not suffered any disability and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability.
Further he has stated that, the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before completion of full treatment to the petitioner.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

sentences.text: If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.

Further it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.3 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 15-04-2023 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 26-03-2025, which is after lapse of one year and eleven months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.

Further, it is pertinent to note that, P.W.3 has clearly admitted in his cross- examination that, the petitioner is a student and she will be having no difficulties in her studies, the fracture sustained by the petitioner is at the region in between the hip joint and the knee joint, the said fracture is united and implants in situ.

Therefore, in such circumstances and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that,
considering the disability of 11% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 11% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.

sentences.text: 22. Discomfort, inconvenience and loss of earnings to the parents during the period of hospitalization:
In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injury i.e., fracture shaft of right femur and for the said injury the petitioner has undergone surgery i.e. CRIF with TENS nailing under GA.
As per Ex.P.9 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 4 days in Sri Priya Nursing Home, Kuppam.
During the period of hospitalization of the petitioner, her parents would have definitely undergone some discomfort, inconvenience and loss of earnings.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/- under this particular head would be just and reasonable.
23. Medical and incidental expenses during the period of hospitalization:

The petitioner has deposed that, she has incurred expenses of Rs.1,50,000/- towards medical, conveyance, food &
nourishment, attendant charges and other incidental charge.
In order to prove the same, she has produced 4 medical bills, as per Ex.P.10.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the parents of petitioner have spent an amount of Rs.41,500/- towards her medical expenses.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.41,500/- under the head of medical expenses.
24. Food and nourishment:
As per Ex.P.9 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 4 days in Sri Priya Nursing Home, Kuppam.
Her parents might have spent some amount towards food and nourishment during that period.

Therefore, compensation of Rs.800 x 4 =
Rs.3,200/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
25. Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Venkatapuram, Santhipuram Mandal,
Cheemanapalle, Karlagatta, Chittoor, Santhipuram, Andhra Pradesh, the accident has taken place on Dommasandra-Chandapura road, near Ramasagara Village, Sarjapura Hobli, Anekal Taluk,
Bengaluru Urban District and she has taken treatment at Sri Priya Nursing Home, Kuppam.
Taking into consideration the distance in between the above places, compensation of Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
26. Future medical expenses:
The P.W.3 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants, which would cost approximately Rs.30,000/-.
But, admittedly the P.W.3 has not issued estimation of cost for the said surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,04,700/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-), from the date of petition till its realization.
28. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle bearing No.KL-56-P-0849.

Further, as per the true copy of reply given by the owner of offending vehicle, to the notice issued by the investigation officer under Sec.133 of Motor Vehicles Act, which is marked as Ex.P.7, the driver of offending vehicle by name Farooq S/o Abdul Rehman was holding valid and effective driving licence bearing No.46/12061/2015 to drive the said vehicle and it is valid from 14-03-2017 to 16-10-2035.
The policy issued by the respondent No.1 bearing No.OG-23- 1607-1801-00000464, in respect of offending Innova car, was valid from 22-10-2022 to 21-10-2023.

As such, the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.1 in respect of offending vehicle was valid as on the date of accident i.e.
15-04-2023.
There is no evidence on record to show that, there is breach of any terms and conditions of the insurance policy issued by the insured/respondent No.1.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KL-56-P- 0849 the accident in question has taken place.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.1 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons,
holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,04,700/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-), from the date of petition till its realization, from the respondent No.1, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
29. Issue No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.4,04,700/- (Rupees four lakh four thousand and seven hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The Suryanagar Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
The rider of the motorcycle was wholly and solely responsible for the alleged accident.
On the contrary, the driver of the Innova car bearing No.KL-56-P-0849 was no way responsible for the alleged accident.
Further it is contended that, the Innova car bearing Reg. No.KL-56-P-0849 was used in a public place without having a valid permit and fitness certificate and thereby violated the terms and conditions of the contract of insurance policy and also against the provisions of Motor Vehicles Act.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
It seeks protection under Section 149(2) of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has denied the age of the petitioner,
injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by her.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 15-04-2023 at about 5.30 p.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Innova Car bearing Reg.
No.KL-56-P- 0849 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?

Therefore, in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, she has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 15-04-2023 at about 5.30 p.m., on Dommasandra-Chandapura road, near Ramasagara Village, Sarjapura Hobli, Anekal Taluk,
Bengaluru Urban District, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Innova car bearing Reg. No.KL-56- P-0849.

4 12.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-HZ-6787 and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of Innova car bearing Reg. No.KL-56-P-0849.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records,
regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident,
negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
Suguna R vs Bajaj All Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7893000/
5 14.
15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.
The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.
Therefore, in such circumstances and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that,
considering the disability of 11% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 11% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
As such, the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.1 in respect of offending vehicle was valid as on the date of accident i.e.
15-04-2023.
There is no evidence on record to show that, there is breach of any terms and conditions of the insurance policy issued by the insured/respondent No.1.
Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KL-56-P- 0849 the accident in question has taken place.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.

In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.1 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons,
holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,04,700/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-), from the date of petition till its realization, from the respondent No.1, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
